chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
"Do not eat the jarri (a type of fish or meat) and the thihal (a type of fish or meat), for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) disliked it."
And he said, "Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him) - it is forbidden to eat the jarri and jumma' from the fish."
He said, "And I asked him about what is found of fish floating on the water or thrown up by the sea dead, and he said, 'Do not eat it.'"

19 - From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), 'People differ with me regarding the rabitha, so what do you command me regarding it?' He wrote (peace be upon him), 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الرَّبِيثَا: Rabitha, a type of fish or food item
key_terms.الطِّحَالَ: Thihal, another specific type of fish or meat
key_terms.الْجِرِّيَّ: Jarri, a specific type of fish or meat mentioned in hadith
key_terms.طَافِياً: Floating, describing the state of the dead fish
key_terms.مَيِّتاً: Dead, describing the state of the fish

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating fish that are found floating dead in water or on the shore?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the prohibition of *jarri* and *thihal* by linking it to both the Prophet’s personal preference (*karah*) and the authoritative *Kitab Ali*, while extending the ruling to fish that die naturally in water (*maytah*). The inclusion of *rabitha* as permissible highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding marine life, distinguishing between specific species and general conditions of death. These rulings reflect the broader Shia emphasis on textual evidence from the Ahl al-Bayt in clarifying dietary laws beyond the general Quranic permissibility of sea food.
